\[
x(ax+1)\ge 0 .
\]

The zeros are at \(x=0\) and \(x=-\frac1a\;(a\neq0)\).  
The sign of the product gives

* **If \(a>0\):** \(x\ge0\) or \(x\le-\frac1a\).  
  Hence \(\displaystyle D=(-\infty,-\frac1a]\cup[0,\infty)\).  
  This domain contains negative numbers, while the range of a square‑root is \([0,\infty)\).  
  Then \(D\neq\text{Range}\).  So no \(a>0\) works.

* **If \(a=0\):** \(f(x)=\sqrt{x}\).  
  \(\displaystyle D=[0,\infty)\) and \(\displaystyle \text{Range}=[0,\infty)\).  
  Thus \(a=0\) satisfies the condition.

* **If \(a<0\):** Let \(a=-c\;(c>0)\).  
  Then \(-\frac1a=\frac1c>0\) and  

  \[
  D=[0,\tfrac1c].
  \]

  On this interval  

  \[
  f(x)=\sqrt{x(1-cx)}.
  \]

  The radicand \(u(x)=x(1-cx)=-c\bigl(x-\tfrac1{2c}\bigr)^{2}+\tfrac1{4c}\) attains its maximum
  at \(x=\tfrac1{2c}\) with

  \[
  u_{\max}=\frac1{4c}=\frac{\tfrac1c}{4}.
  \]

  Hence  

  \[
  \text{Range}= \bigl[0,\sqrt{u_{\max}}\bigr]=\Bigl[0,\frac{\sqrt{\tfrac1c}}{2}\Bigr]
          =\Bigl[0,\frac{1}{2\sqrt{c}}\Bigr].
  \]

  For the range to equal the domain \([0,\tfrac1c]\) we need  

  \[
  \frac{1}{2\sqrt{c}}=\frac1c\;\Longrightarrow\;c=\frac14.
  \]

  Thus \(c=\frac14\) and \(a=-c=-4\).

  When \(a=-4\),

  \[
  D=[0,\tfrac14],\qquad f(x)=\sqrt{x-\!4x^{2}},
  \]

  whose maximum value on the domain is \(\frac14\) (attained at \(x=\frac18\)).
  The function is continuous on \([0,\frac14]\) and takes every value between 0 and
  \(\frac14\); hence \(\text{Range}=[0,\frac14]=D\).

Therefore the only values of \(a\) for which the domain and range of \(f\) coincide are  

\[
\boxed{a=0\ \text{or}\ a=-4 }.
